minutes.summary: The board handled a one-day alcohol license, a Council on Aging appointment, a peddler permit and a skateboard park fundraising update. It then worked through earth removal permit renewals for Keating and Powell, reviewed amendments to its policies, set a fall special town meeting date, and heard the town accountant's FY18 year-end revenue review.

what_happened.line: The Select Board renewed most earth removal permits for three months, did not renew two, and renewed three others to August 31, 2019.
The board extended the Powell permit three months, with closure plan requirements and parcel 8 requirements folded into site plan review.
The board approved its amended selectmen policy sections as amended at the meeting.
The board set the fall special town meeting for Tuesday, November 13th, and postponed the Council on Aging contract to September 4th.
The town accountant reported FY18 revenues above estimates and expenditures below, pointing to a larger free cash certification.

why_it_matters: Short three-month earth removal renewals keep gravel operations under regular board review, and two permits were not renewed.
Higher-than-estimated revenue and lower spending point to more free cash, which Town Meeting may be asked to use for the budget or to lower the tax burden.
Recycling terms are being renegotiated because mixed paper and glass now cost money to dispose of, which could raise the town's trash and recycling costs.
watch_next: Special town meeting on Tuesday, November 13th.
Council on Aging contract returns to the board on September 4th.
